# Read the brief

Most failed calls come from one rule that was skipped. Read every line of every file in
`input/`. Do not search by keyword instead of reading. Use only what the inputs say: never
copy a rule, value or sentence from anything else, and never guess a missing value.

## 1. Read
- Read each brief file from the first line to the last. If a file is long, read it in parts
  until you have seen every line.
- Read the tool API file: every tool, every request field, every allowed value, every response
  field. The tool names are fixed; fields and allowed values may differ from what you expect.

## 2. Resolve the documents (raw material)
The brief may be several documents: a mail, a policy extract, a memo, a code list.
- List each document with its date or order.
- A later memo or mail that changes a rule wins over the earlier document, unless it says it
  applies only to some cases. A code list defines allowed values and their meaning.
- Write every conflict and its winner, with both quotes, into `conflicts` in rules.json.

## 3. Write work/rules.json, the rule ledger
A list. One entry per atomic rule (one condition, one action):
    {"id": "R12", "quote": "<exact words from the brief>", "file": "<file name>",
     "kind": "<opening | who_is_on_line | third_party | identity | debt_statement | dates |
              amounts | persuasion | read_back | recording | special_case | closing |
              required_sentence | forbidden | other>",
     "rule": "<the rule in one plain sentence>",
     "implemented_by": ""}            filled in by the design step
- The quote must appear word for word in the file. The check step verifies this.
- Split compound rules. "Say X, ask nothing else, and close as Y" is three rules.
- Precedence ("this comes before rule N", "takes priority") is its own rule.
- Numbers, dates, limits, counts and exact sentences go in the rule, unchanged.

## 4. Write work/spec.json, the parameters
The exact keys are in builder/reference/SPEC.md (read it in full). Fill every field the inputs give; leave a field out when the inputs say nothing about it,
and add a `gaps` list naming each missing item. Never invent a value.
    call_variables        names and meaning of the variables every call starts with
    opening               the first sentence's required content; who to ask for and how
    forbidden_before_verification   words that must not be said before identity passes
    confirmation_words    what counts as confirming identity, and what does not
    identity              questions in order, the tool field values for each, answer
                          format per question (date / digits:N / year / text), numeric date
                          order, wrong-answer limit and what does not count as wrong
    calendar              business days, weekend days, holidays, how "Nth business day after
                          today" is counted, "this"/"next" weekday meaning
    bands                 per band: days-late range, deadline rule, persuasion attempts
    products              per product type: spoken name, floor field, any other rule
    persuasion            what each attempt proposes (amount and date)
    callback              window (days and hours, inclusive or not), retries allowed
    special_cases         each: trigger words, action, tool call, outcome/reason, precedence
    outcomes              the outcome table: outcome, reason, when
    notes                 when notes are written, reasons, when never to write them
    required_sentences    exact sentences, with when they must be said
    restricted_words      words the brief forbids in one situation and requires in another
                          (for example a word allowed only after a tool succeeded)
    tool_failures         what to do when each tool fails, and how many retries
    multi_product         ordering, one read-back or many, per-product counting
    tools                 per tool: the API fields to fill from call variables, and which the
                          agent fills

## 4b. Words with a condition
Look for every rule that allows a word or a claim only after something happens (for example
a claim allowed only after a tool succeeded). Put each such word in `restricted_words`. If a
required sentence (the opening, a fixed line) needs the same idea, write it in other words in
the spec, and note the paraphrase in rules.json. Keep the paraphrase plain and as close to the
original as possible, so a reader still recognises the required statement: prefer a related
form of the same word (a noun instead of a verb) over an unusual synonym. Never put such a word in a line spoken
before the condition can be true.

## 4c. A case that is not a collection call
If the case is another kind of call (see design-agent step 0), spec.json holds whatever your
own generator needs, in the same spirit: every value, sentence, condition and branch from the
documents, with the document it came from, and conflicts resolved (the later or more specific
document wins; say which). rules.json is the same as above. Read the test data as well: it
shows edge cases (errors, empty lists, look-alike values) the agent must handle.

## 5. Check before moving on
- Every line of every brief file is covered by at least one rule or is plainly descriptive.
- Every rule with a number, date or sentence has it in spec.json too.
- Every fixed line (`line`, `say`, `first_line`, the opening) is spoken word for word and the
  model adds nothing to it. So it must hold EVERYTHING the brief requires at that moment, in
  the brief's order: a special case whose action is "one sentence of sympathy, then offer X"
  needs a `line` with the sympathy sentence AND the offer. Read each line next to its rule.
- `gaps` lists anything the design step must handle without a value. Prefer the safe
  behaviour: do less, record nothing uncertain, close honestly.

Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, card, amount and address in this pack is synthetic.

## When

The case opens Sunday 11 October, 17:00 UTC (20:00 Istanbul). Submissions close Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).

## The scenario

Freya Bank wants its phone line to answer one of its most common calls with a voice assistant: "how much is my credit card statement debt?". The caller has already passed the bank's phone menu (IVR). The menu has checked who they are and hands the call to the assistant with the customer number. The assistant finds the right card, reads the statement debt in Turkish lira, US dollars, euros and pounds sterling, and says when it is due.

In the same call the customer may want two more things: move their statement date to another week, or get the statement sent to the e-mail address the bank has on file. A customer who wants to pay or who asks for a person is handed to a human agent. The calls are in Turkish.

The bank did not write a clean specification. It sent what it had: an analysis document, the announcements its phone menu reads today, a flow drawing, service descriptions, an integration document, its mails to our team, a list of abbreviations and an FAQ. They were written months apart and they do not always agree.

## What you build

1. **First, your own mock of the bank's services**, on Cloudflare Workers. Same paths, same field names, same request and response shapes as the bank's integration document (section 6). For the bank's test customers it returns exactly the answers listed in the pack, HTTP status included. Deploy it before you run your builder and keep it running until the results are out: our simulated customers reach your mock through the tools in your workflow, so a Worker that is down fails those conversations.
2. **Then the phone agent, built by your builder.** Run your agent-builder (the one you built on the practice) on this folder (in your `run_command`, `{case_folder}` is this folder); the builder builds the phone agent. No manual edits to what it builds. You may fix bugs in your builder, but do not hard-code this case into it. The phone agent's tools call your mock. It runs on Freya LLM, the only model on staging. Every builder rule on the event page holds here too.

Every call gives the phone agent two variables:

- `customerNumber`: the 8-digit customer number from the phone menu. The agent never asks for it.
- `now`: the date and time of the call, Istanbul time, for example `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`. Every date decision uses `now`, never the system clock.

## Inputs

- `README.md`: the pack overview: what each folder is, the two variables.
- `sources/emails/`: the bank's mail threads with our team, as received, with their attachments in `attachments/` (three versions of the analysis document).
- `sources/documents/`: the documents the bank handed over: flow drawing, current phone-menu announcements, abbreviations, FAQ, two versions of the data models, service examples and the IVR integration document.
- `sources/meetings/`: excerpts from the recordings of meetings with the bank, and the meeting notes.
- `test-environment/`: the bank's test customers (`test-customers.md`, `test-customers.json`) your mock must serve, and the rules of the test environment.
- `example-scenarios.md`: six example conversations (two ordinary, two edge, two adversarial) of the kind we score with. The rest stay hidden.
- `cloudflare-mock/`: how to run and deploy a Worker, with a one-endpoint example. The bank's services you write yourself.

## How you are scored

Your phone agent is tested with simulated customers you never see. The workflow your builder made is reviewed too. In the simulations your agent's tools call your mock, so a wrong or unreachable mock fails those conversations. Traces are not scored; we read them to check the agent came out of your builder without hand edits.

get confirmation# Mock service with Cloudflare Workers

Your flow's tools call a mock service that you write, instead of the real bank service. You publish this service as a free Cloudflare Worker. The `example/` folder here only shows the pattern: a Worker with a single endpoint (`POST /ping`). You will write the statement-debt services yourself.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or later
- A free Cloudflare account (dash.cloudflare.com)
- Wrangler (Cloudflare's command-line tool): runs without installing, via `npx wrangler ...`

## 1. Run the example locally

```bash
cd example
npx wrangler dev
```

The Worker opens at `http://localhost:8787`. Try it from another terminal:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8787/ping \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"kod": "A1"}'
```

The response is the same as `example/example-response.json`. For a code that does not exist it returns `404` and `{"hata": "kayıt bulunamadı"}`.

## 2. Publish it

```bash
npx wrangler login      # grant access to your Cloudflare account in the browser
npx wrangler deploy
```

The output shows the Worker address: `https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev`. To change the name, change the `name` field in `wrangler.toml`. Run `npx wrangler deploy` again whenever the code changes; the address stays the same.

Check after publishing:

```bash
curl -s https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/health
```

## 3. Connect the tool in the Freya flow to the Worker

1. Add an API tool to the flow.
2. Enter the method and address: `POST https://<your-worker-name>.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/<path>`. For the statement services, use the same path as under the bank's base address in `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` (for example `/voice/v1/cards.list`).
3. In the request body, write variables in the form `{{variable_name}}`. Example: `{"data": {"customerNo": "{{customerNumber}}", "aiFlow": "..."}, "call": {...}}`. During the call, the variable's value is substituted in.
4. Take the fields you will use in the flow from the response into variables.

The "Test API Request" button in the panel may send the text `{{customerNumber}}` as is, without filling in the variables. In this case the example Worker returns a valid record instead of an error (`isTemplateVariable`). Doing the same in your own services makes testing easier.

## When writing your own services

- Endpoints, request and response fields must match `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` exactly: the same path, the same field names (`data`/`call` request body, `data`/`result` response), the same date and amount format. The test customers' responses are in `../test-environment/test-customers.json`, explained in `../test-environment/test-customers.md`.
- Keep customer and card data in a table inside the Worker file (like `RECORDS` in the example). No database is needed.
- For a customer or card that is not found, return the error response from the contract; do not return made-up data.
- Responses should return data only (amount, date, status). The flow builds the sentence to be said to the customer.
- Do not put secret keys or real personal data in it; the Worker address is public.

# Credit cards: statements and payments

Answers to the questions we hear most often about your Yıldız credit card statement and how to pay it. Can't find what you need? Scroll to the bottom for ways to reach us.

---

**When will I get my statement?**

Once a month, on your statement date. Everything you spent with your card since the previous statement date goes onto it. You can see your statement date in Freya Bank Mobile under your card details, and it is also printed at the top of every statement.

**Can I change my statement date?**

Yes. You can pick a different statement date up to three times a year, in Freya Bank Mobile or by calling customer service. The new date applies from your next statement onwards. Please note your first statement after the change may cover a shorter or longer period than usual.

**How do I get my statement by e-mail?**

Just tell us where you'd like it sent. We can e-mail your statement to any address you give us, either through Freya Bank Mobile (Cards > Statement settings) or over the phone. E-mailed statements come as a PDF.

**I didn't receive my statement. What should I do?**

First check your spam or junk folder. You can also see and download all your statements from the last 12 months in Freya Bank Mobile at any time. If it's still missing, contact customer service and we'll send it again.

**What is the minimum payment?**

It is the smallest amount you need to pay by the due date to keep your card in good standing. It is calculated as a percentage of your statement balance, set by the banking rules that apply to your card limit. The exact amount is shown on your statement and in the app.

**What happens if I only pay the minimum?**

Your card stays in good standing, but interest is charged on the part of the balance you didn't pay. Paying the full statement balance is the only way to avoid interest.

**And if I pay less than the minimum, or nothing?**

Late payment interest is charged and it may affect your credit record. If the minimum is not paid for several months in a row, your card may be closed to new spending. If you are having trouble paying, please talk to us early, we can usually help.

**When is my payment due?**

Your due date is shown on your statement, usually about 10 days after the statement date. If the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday, it moves to the next working day.

**I spent in dollars, euros or pounds. How is that shown?**

Spending in a foreign currency is shown on your statement in that currency, separately from your Turkish lira spending. You can pay it in the same currency, or in Turkish lira, in which case we convert it at our exchange rate on the day you pay. Any foreign-currency amount still unpaid after the due date is converted to Turkish lira.

**How can I pay my card?**

- In Freya Bank Mobile: Cards > select your card > Pay. You can pay from any of your Freya Bank accounts.
- At any Freya Bank branch, in cash or from your account.
- At Freya Bank ATMs, with or without a card.
- Automatically: set up automatic payment and we'll take the minimum or the full amount from your account on the due date.

Payments in the app or at an ATM show on your card straight away. (Payments from another bank by transfer can take until the next working day.)

**Can I pay my card over the phone?**

You can check your balance and statement details on the phone line. For payments we recommend Freya Bank Mobile, it's the quickest way.

**Can I split my statement into instalments?**

For some purchases, yes, depending on the merchant and your card. Eligible transactions show an "Instalment" option in Freya Bank Mobile. Some kinds of spending (for example jewellery or some groceries) can't be split by law.

**There's a transaction on my statement I don't recognise. What do I do?**

Please contact customer service as soon as possible, by phone or through the "Messages" section in Freya Bank Mobile. Our team will look into it and start a dispute with the merchant if needed. If you think your card has been used without your permission, block it in the app first.

**Is my statement the same for all my cards?**

If you have more than one Yıldız card, each card gets its own statement, unless you have asked for a joint statement. Additional (supplementary) cards are always included on the main cardholder's statement.

# Voice assistant: statement and debt services, service contract

Author: Mert Koç, Integration Architecture, Freya Bank (mert.koc@freyabank.example)
Date: 1 October 2026
Distribution: Selin Aydın, Kerem Yalçın, Burcu Tan (Freya Bank); Deniz Arı (Freya)

> Mert: This is the contract the voice assistant integrates against for the statement / debt use case. It covers only the seven services the assistant calls. Everything about how the call reaches the assistant and how it goes back to the phone menu is Burcu's side and is not in here. If something below disagrees with what you see in the test environment, tell me and I'll check which side is wrong.

## 1. Before you start

- The caller is already identified when the assistant picks up. The phone menu hands over the **customer number** with the call, so there is no customer search service in this contract. Start from `cards.list`.
- Every service is `POST`, JSON in, JSON out, UTF-8.
- Base address for all seven:

```
https://api.freyabank.example/voice/v1/
```

  So the card list is `POST https://api.freyabank.example/voice/v1/cards.list`, and so on.
- Dates are strings in `dd.MM.yyyy` (e.g. `"05.11.2026"`). Amounts are JSON numbers with a dot as decimal separator (`5000.13`), never formatted strings. Do not round them.
- Turning numbers and dates into speech is the assistant's job. The services return raw values only, no sentences meant to be read to the caller (the `messageText` in errors is for logs, please don't read it out).

## 2. Access token

The services sit behind our API gateway. You need a bearer token first.

```
POST https://api.freyabank.example/oauth2/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=<client id>&client_secret=<client secret>&scope=voice.statement
```

Answer:

```json
{
  "access_token": "<token>",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 1800
}
```

Then on every service call:

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `Authorization` | `Bearer <token>` |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |
| `Accept` | `application/json` |

The token belongs to the integration (service account), not to the caller. Cache it and get a fresh one when it runs out; don't fetch one per call. Client id and secret: I'll send them over the secure channel, not by e-mail.

(Test environment: the token and headers are not checked there. Send them anyway so nothing changes when we switch.)

## 3. Envelope

### Request

```json
{
  "data": { "...service fields..." },
  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
}
```

`data` carries the fields of each service (section 5). `call` is call metadata we log on our side; nothing in this contract depends on it and the test environment ignores it.

### Response

Every answer has a `result` object. Successful answers also have `data`.

```json
{
  "data": { "...service fields..." },
  "result": {
    "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0002",
    "returnCode": "1",
    "messageText": "Success",
    "code": "1",
    "message": "Success",
    "type": null,
    "details": {
      "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0002",
      "rootCause": null,
      "errorOrigin": null
    }
  }
}
```

Success = HTTP 200 and `result.returnCode` is `"1"`. Anything else is an error, see section 4. `guid` is our trace id; if you open a ticket with us, give us the `guid`.

## 4. Errors

Error answers have **no `data` object**, only `result`:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0086",
    "returnCode": "FBE00099",
    "messageText": "Teknik hata: ABORTED: ",
    "code": "FBE00099",
    "message": "Teknik hata: ABORTED: ",
    "type": "ERROR",
    "details": {
      "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0086",
      "rootCause": "TechnicalError",
      "errorOrigin": "ivr-gateway-test:ivr-channel-v0"
    }
  }
}
```

`returnCode` and `code` always carry the same value, and so do `messageText` and `message`. `type` is `"ERROR"` or `"WARNING"`. `rootCause` and `errorOrigin` are diagnostic strings; log them, don't branch on them.

Codes you can get:

| HTTP | `code` | `type` | When | Services |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR` | `ERROR` | A required field is missing or empty (message names the field, e.g. `"card number cannot be empty"`) | all |
| 401 | (gateway) | | Token missing or expired. Get a new token and retry once | all |
| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_102` | `WARNING` | Customer has no valid card (message: `"Müşteriye ait geçerli kart bilgisi bulunamadı."`) | `cards.list` |
| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_120` | `WARNING` | Card not found | `cards.balance` |
| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_121` | `WARNING` | Card not found | `statement.week.get` |
| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_107` | `WARNING` | No statement document to send (message: `"Pdf dokümanı bulunamadı"`) | `statement.pdf.send` |
| 500 | `FBE00099` | `ERROR` | Technical error on our side (message: `"Teknik hata: ABORTED: "`) | all |

Note on the `cards.list` 404: it's a WARNING, it means "this customer has no card the assistant can work with", not that the service is broken. How the assistant reacts to that vs. a 500 is for Selin's analysis, I'm only flagging that they are different things.

Timeouts: we haven't agreed a client timeout yet. Most answers are well under a second, but under load (and once in the test data) an answer can take longer than ten seconds and still succeed. Open point, see section 7.

## 5. Services

| # | Service | Called with | Gives back |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.1 | `cards.list` | customer number | the customer's cards the assistant may talk about |
| 5.2 | `cards.balance` | card number | statement and due dates, debt per currency |
| 5.3 | `statement.week.get` | card number | the card's current statement week and day, joint statement info |
| 5.4 | `statement.week.decide` | card number + requested week | what the dates *would* be with that week (does not change anything) |
| 5.5 | `statement.week.change` | card number + requested week | changes the statement week |
| 5.6 | `contact.email.get` | customer number | registered e-mail / phone |
| 5.7 | `statement.pdf.send` | customer, card, currency, statement date, address | sends the statement PDF by e-mail |

1	# The final case: Freya Bank, credit card statement debt
2	
3	Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, card, amount and address in this pack is synthetic.
4	
5	## When
6	
7	The case opens Sunday 11 October, 17:00 UTC (20:00 Istanbul). Submissions close Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).
8	
9	## The scenario
10	
11	Freya Bank wants its phone line to answer one of its most common calls with a voice assistant: "how much is my credit card statement debt?". The caller has already passed the bank's phone menu (IVR). The menu has checked who they are and hands the call to the assistant with the customer number. The assistant finds the right card, reads the statement debt in Turkish lira, US dollars, euros and pounds sterling, and says when it is due.
12	
13	In the same call the customer may want two more things: move their statement date to another week, or get the statement sent to the e-mail address the bank has on file. A customer who wants to pay or who asks for a person is handed to a human agent. The calls are in Turkish.
14	
15	The bank did not write a clean specification. It sent what it had: an analysis document, the announcements its phone menu reads today, a flow drawing, service descriptions, an integration document, its mails to our team, a list of abbreviations and an FAQ. They were written months apart and they do not always agree.
16	
17	## What you build
18	
19	1. **First, your own mock of the bank's services**, on Cloudflare Workers. Same paths, same field names, same request and response shapes as the bank's integration document (section 6). For the bank's test customers it returns exactly the answers listed in the pack, HTTP status included. Deploy it before you run your builder and keep it running until the results are out: our simulated customers reach your mock through the tools in your workflow, so a Worker that is down fails those conversations.
20	2. **Then the phone agent, built by your builder.** Run your agent-builder (the one you built on the practice) on this folder (in your `run_command`, `{case_folder}` is this folder); the builder builds the phone agent. No manual edits to what it builds. You may fix bugs in your builder, but do not hard-code this case into it. The phone agent's tools call your mock. It runs on Freya LLM, the only model on staging. Every builder rule on the event page holds here too.
21	
22	Every call gives the phone agent two variables:
23	
24	- `customerNumber`: the 8-digit customer number from the phone menu. The agent never asks for it.
25	- `now`: the date and time of the call, Istanbul time, for example `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`. Every date decision uses `now`, never the system clock.

164	Your flow's tools call a mock service that you write, instead of the real bank service. You publish this service as a free Cloudflare Worker. The `example/` folder here only shows the pattern: a Worker with a single endpoint (`POST /ping`). You will write the statement-debt services yourself.
165	
166	## Requirements
167	
168	- Node.js 18 or later
169	- A free Cloudflare account (dash.cloudflare.com)
170	- Wrangler (Cloudflare's command-line tool): runs without installing, via `npx wrangler ...`
171	
172	## 1. Run the example locally
173	
174	```bash
175	cd example
176	npx wrangler dev
177	```
178	
179	The Worker opens at `http://localhost:8787`. Try it from another terminal:
180	
181	```bash
182	curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8787/ping \
183	  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
184	  -d '{"kod": "A1"}'
185	```
186	
187	The response is the same as `example/example-response.json`. For a code that does not exist it returns `404` and `{"hata": "kayıt bulunamadı"}`.
188	
189	## 2. Publish it
190	
191	```bash
192	npx wrangler login      # grant access to your Cloudflare account in the browser
193	npx wrangler deploy
194	```
195	
196	The output shows the Worker address: `https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev`. To change the name, change the `name` field in `wrangler.toml`. Run `npx wrangler deploy` again whenever the code changes; the address stays the same.
197

202	```

204	## 3. Connect the tool in the Freya flow to the Worker
205	
206	1. Add an API tool to the flow.
207	2. Enter the method and address: `POST https://<your-worker-name>.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/<path>`. For the statement services, use the same path as under the bank's base address in `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` (for example `/voice/v1/cards.list`).
208	3. In the request body, write variables in the form `{{variable_name}}`. Example: `{"data": {"customerNo": "{{customerNumber}}", "aiFlow": "..."}, "call": {...}}`. During the call, the variable's value is substituted in.
209	4. Take the fields you will use in the flow from the response into variables.
210	
211	The "Test API Request" button in the panel may send the text `{{customerNumber}}` as is, without filling in the variables. In this case the example Worker returns a valid record instead of an error (`isTemplateVariable`). Doing the same in your own services makes testing easier.
212	
213	## When writing your own services
214	
215	- Endpoints, request and response fields must match `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` exactly: the same path, the same field names (`data`/`call` request body, `data`/`result` response), the same date and amount format. The test customers' responses are in `../test-environment/test-customers.json`, explained in `../test-environment/test-customers.md`.
216	- Keep customer and card data in a table inside the Worker file (like `RECORDS` in the example). No database is needed.
217	- For a customer or card that is not found, return the error response from the contract; do not return made-up data.
218	- Responses should return data only (amount, date, status). The flow builds the sentence to be said to the customer.
219	- Do not put secret keys or real personal data in it; the Worker address is public.

226	# Credit cards: statements and payments
227	
228	Answers to the questions we hear most often about your Yıldız credit card statement and how to pay it. Can't find what you need? Scroll to the bottom for ways to reach us.
229	
230	---
231	
232	**When will I get my statement?**
233	
234	Once a month, on your statement date. Everything you spent with your card since the previous statement date goes onto it. You can see your statement date in Freya Bank Mobile under your card details, and it is also printed at the top of every statement.
235	
236	**Can I change my statement date?**
237	
238	Yes. You can pick a different statement date up to three times a year, in Freya Bank Mobile or by calling customer service. The new date applies from your next statement onwards. Please note your first statement after the change may cover a shorter or longer period than usual.
239	
240	**How do I get my statement by e-mail?**
241	
242	Just tell us where you'd like it sent. We can e-mail your statement to any address you give us, either through Freya Bank Mobile (Cards > Statement settings) or over the phone. E-mailed statements come as a PDF.
243	
244	**I didn't receive my statement. What should I do?**
245	
246	First check your spam or junk folder. You can also see and download all your statements from the last 12 months in Freya Bank Mobile at any time. If it's still missing, contact customer service and we'll send it again.
247	
248	**What is the minimum payment?**
249	
250	It is the smallest amount you need to pay by the due date to keep your card in good standing. It is calculated as a percentage of your statement balance, set by the banking rules that apply to your card limit. The exact amount is shown on your statement and in the app.
251	
252	**What happens if I only pay the minimum?**
253	
254	Your card stays in good standing, but interest is charged on the part of the balance you didn't pay. Paying the full statement balance is the only way to avoid interest.
255	
256	**And if I pay less than the minimum, or nothing?**
257	
258	Late payment interest is charged and it may affect your credit record. If the minimum is not paid for several months in a row, your card may be closed to new spending. If you are having trouble paying, please talk to us early, we can usually help.
259	
260	**When is my payment due?**
261	
262	Your due date is shown on your statement, usually about 10 days after the statement date. If the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday, it moves to the next working day.
263	
264	**I spent in dollars, euros or pounds. How is that shown?**
265	
266	Spending in a foreign currency is shown on your statement in that currency, separately from your Turkish lira spending. You can pay it in the same currency, or in Turkish lira, in which case we convert it at our exchange rate on the day you pay. Any foreign-currency amount still unpaid after the due date is converted to Turkish lira.
267	
268	**How can I pay my card?**
269	
270	- In Freya Bank Mobile: Cards > select your card > Pay. You can pay from any of your Freya Bank accounts.
271	- At any Freya Bank branch, in cash or from your account.
272	- At Freya Bank ATMs, with or without a card.
273	- Automatically: set up automatic payment and we'll take the minimum or the full amount from your account on the due date.
274	
275	Payments in the app or at an ATM show on your card straight away. (Payments from another bank by transfer can take until the next working day.)
276	
277	**Can I pay my card over the phone?**
278	
279	You can check your balance and statement details on the phone line. For payments we recommend Freya Bank Mobile, it's the quickest way.
280	
281	**Can I split my statement into instalments?**
282	
283	For some purchases, yes, depending on the merchant and your card. Eligible transactions show an "Instalment" option in Freya Bank Mobile. Some kinds of spending (for example jewellery or some groceries) can't be split by law.
284	
285	**There's a transaction on my statement I don't recognise. What do I do?**
286	
287	Please contact customer service as soon as possible, by phone or through the "Messages" section in Freya Bank Mobile. Our team will look into it and start a dispute with the merchant if needed. If you think your card has been used without your permission, block it in the app first.
288	
289	**Is my statement the same for all my cards?**
290	
291	If you have more than one Yıldız card, each card gets its own statement, unless you have asked for a joint statement. Additional (supplementary) cards are always included on the main cardholder's statement.

361	Date: 1 October 2026

364	> Mert: This is the contract the voice assistant integrates against for the statement / debt use case. It covers only the seven services the assistant calls. Everything about how the call reaches the assistant and how it goes back to the phone menu is Burcu's side and is not in here. If something below disagrees with what you see in the test environment, tell me and I'll check which side is wrong.
365	
366	## 1. Before you start
367	
368	- The caller is already identified when the assistant picks up. The phone menu hands over the **customer number** with the call, so there is no customer search service in this contract. Start from `cards.list`.
369	- Every service is `POST`, JSON in, JSON out, UTF-8.
370	- Base address for all seven:
371	
372	```
373	https://api.freyabank.example/voice/v1/
374	```
375	
376	  So the card list is `POST https://api.freyabank.example/voice/v1/cards.list`, and so on.
377	- Dates are strings in `dd.MM.yyyy` (e.g. `"05.11.2026"`). Amounts are JSON numbers with a dot as decimal separator (`5000.13`), never formatted strings. Do not round them.
378	- Turning numbers and dates into speech is the assistant's job. The services return raw values only, no sentences meant to be read to the caller (the `messageText` in errors is for logs, please don't read it out).
379	
380	## 2. Access token
381	
382	The services sit behind our API gateway. You need a bearer token first.
383	
384	```
385	POST https://api.freyabank.example/oauth2/token
386	Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
387	
388	grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=<client id>&client_secret=<client secret>&scope=voice.statement
389	```
390	
391	Answer:
392	
393	```json
394	{
395	  "access_token": "<token>",
396	  "token_type": "Bearer",
397	  "expires_in": 1800
398	}
399	```
400	
401	Then on every service call:
402	
403	| Header | Value |
404	|---|---|
405	| `Authorization` | `Bearer <token>` |
406	| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |
407	| `Accept` | `application/json` |
408	
409	The token belongs to the integration (service account), not to the caller. Cache it and get a fresh one when it runs out; don't fetch one per call. Client id and secret: I'll send them over the secure channel, not by e-mail.
410	
411	(Test environment: the token and headers are not checked there. Send them anyway so nothing changes when we switch.)
412	
413	## 3. Envelope
414	
415	### Request
416	
417	```json
418	{
419	  "data": { "...service fields..." },
420	  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
421	}
422	```
423	
424	`data` carries the fields of each service (section 5). `call` is call metadata we log on our side; nothing in this contract depends on it and the test environment ignores it.
425	
426	### Response
427	
428	Every answer has a `result` object. Successful answers also have `data`.
429	
430	```json
431	{
432	  "data": { "...service fields..." },
433	  "result": {
434	    "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0002",
435	    "returnCode": "1",
436	    "messageText": "Success",
437	    "code": "1",
438	    "message": "Success",
439	    "type": null,
440	    "details": {
441	      "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0002",
442	      "rootCause": null,
443	      "errorOrigin": null
444	    }
445	  }
446	}
447	```
448	
449	Success = HTTP 200 and `result.returnCode` is `"1"`. Anything else is an error, see section 4. `guid` is our trace id; if you open a ticket with us, give us the `guid`.
450	
451	## 4. Errors
452	
453	Error answers have **no `data` object**, only `result`:
454	
455	```json
456	{
457	  "result": {
458	    "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0086",
459	    "returnCode": "FBE00099",
460	    "messageText": "Teknik hata: ABORTED: ",
461	    "code": "FBE00099",
462	    "message": "Teknik hata: ABORTED: ",
463	    "type": "ERROR",
464	    "details": {
465	      "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0086",
466	      "rootCause": "TechnicalError",
467	      "errorOrigin": "ivr-gateway-test:ivr-channel-v0"
468	    }
469	  }
470	}
471	```
472	
473	`returnCode` and `code` always carry the same value, and so do `messageText` and `message`. `type` is `"ERROR"` or `"WARNING"`. `rootCause` and `errorOrigin` are diagnostic strings; log them, don't branch on them.
474	
475	Codes you can get:
476	
477	| HTTP | `code` | `type` | When | Services |
478	|---|---|---|---|---|
479	| 400 | `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR` | `ERROR` | A required field is missing or empty (message names the field, e.g. `"card number cannot be empty"`) | all |
480	| 401 | (gateway) | | Token missing or expired. Get a new token and retry once | all |
481	| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_102` | `WARNING` | Customer has no valid card (message: `"Müşteriye ait geçerli kart bilgisi bulunamadı."`) | `cards.list` |
482	| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_120` | `WARNING` | Card not found | `cards.balance` |
483	| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_121` | `WARNING` | Card not found | `statement.week.get` |
484	| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_107` | `WARNING` | No statement document to send (message: `"Pdf dokümanı bulunamadı"`) | `statement.pdf.send` |
485	| 500 | `FBE00099` | `ERROR` | Technical error on our side (message: `"Teknik hata: ABORTED: "`) | all |
486	
487	Note on the `cards.list` 404: it's a WARNING, it means "this customer has no card the assistant can work with", not that the service is broken. How the assistant reacts to that vs. a 500 is for Selin's analysis, I'm only flagging that they are different things.
488	
489	Timeouts: we haven't agreed a client timeout yet. Most answers are well under a second, but under load (and once in the test data) an answer can take longer than ten seconds and still succeed. Open point, see section 7.

493	| # | Service | Called with | Gives back |

495	| 5.1 | `cards.list` | customer number | the customer's cards the assistant may talk about |

577	
578	```json
579	{
580	  "data": {
581	    "cardNumber": "5400********1234",
582	    "cardNumberLast4": "1234",
583	    "productName": "Yıldız Pratik Classic",

589	      "statementPaymentStatus": "HAS_DEBT",
590	      "transferAmount": 0.0,
591	      "statementDebt": 5000.13,
592	      "minPayment": 2000.05,
593	      "remainingDebt": 5000.13,
594	      "remainingMinPayment": 2000.05,
595	      "currentPeriodExpense": 0.0,
596	      "totalDebt": 5000.13,
597	      "totalDebtPaymentStatus": "HAS_DEBT",

Changing the week on either card moves the shared statement, i.e. both cards.

732	
733	This one changes the card. Call it only after the caller has agreed to the dates from 5.4.

735	Request:
736	
737	```json

740	    "cardNumber": "540000******1234",

743	  },

755	    "responseCode": 0,
756	    "responseMessage": "00",

829

# The final case: Freya Bank, credit card statement debt

Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, card, amount and address in this pack is synthetic.

## When

The case opens Sunday 11 October, 17:00 UTC (20:00 Istanbul). Submissions close Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).

## The scenario

Freya Bank wants its phone line to answer one of its most common calls with a voice assistant: "how much is my credit card statement debt?". The caller has already passed the bank's phone menu (IVR). The menu has checked who they are and hands the call to the assistant with the customer number. The assistant finds the right card, reads the statement debt in Turkish lira, US dollars, euros and pounds sterling, and says when it is due.

In the same call the customer may want two more things: move their statement date to another week, or get the statement sent to the e-mail address the bank has on file. A customer who wants to pay or who asks for a person is handed to a human agent. The calls are in Turkish.

The bank did not write a clean specification. It sent what it had: an analysis document, the announcements its phone menu reads today, a flow drawing, service descriptions, an integration document, its mails to our team, a list of abbreviations and an FAQ. They were written months apart and they do not always agree.

## What you build

1. **First, your own mock of the bank's services**, on Cloudflare Workers. Same paths, same field names, same request and response shapes as the bank's integration document (section 6). For the bank's test customers it returns exactly the answers listed in the pack, HTTP status included. Deploy it before you run your builder and keep it running until the results are out: our simulated customers reach your mock through the tools in your workflow, so a Worker that is down fails those conversations.
2. **Then the phone agent, built by your builder.** Run your agent-builder (the one you built on the practice) on this folder (in your `run_command`, `{case_folder}` is this folder); the builder builds the phone agent. No manual edits to what it builds. You may fix bugs in your builder, but do not hard-code this case into it. The phone agent's tools call your mock. It runs on Freya LLM, the only model on staging. Every builder rule on the event page holds here too.

Every call gives the phone agent two variables:

- `customerNumber`: the 8-digit customer number from the phone menu. The agent never asks for it.
- `now`: the date and time of the call, Istanbul time, for example `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`. Every date decision uses `now`, never the system clock.

## Inputs

- `README.md`: the pack overview: what each folder is, the two variables.
- `sources/emails/`: the bank's mail threads with our team, as received, with their attachments in `attachments/` (three versions of the analysis document).
- `sources/documents/`: the documents the bank handed over: flow drawing, current phone-menu announcements, abbreviations, FAQ, two versions of the data models, service examples and the IVR integration document.
- `sources/meetings/`: excerpts from the recordings of meetings with the bank, and the meeting notes.
- `test-environment/`: the bank's test customers (`test-customers.md`, `test-customers.json`) your mock must serve, and the rules of the test environment.
- `example-scenarios.md`: six example conversations (two ordinary, two edge, two adversarial) of the kind we score with. The rest stay hidden.
- `cloudflare-mock/`: how to run and deploy a Worker, with a one-endpoint example. The bank's services you write yourself.

## How you are scored

Your phone agent is tested with simulated customers you never see. The workflow your builder made is reviewed too. In the simulations your agent's tools call your mock, so a wrong or unreachable mock fails those conversations. Traces are not scored; we read them to check the agent came out of your builder without hand edits.

## What you submit

One `submission.json`: the workflow your builder made, the trace of that builder run (paths relative to the repo) and the address of your mock.

```json
{
  "team": "Your team name",
  "members": [{ "name": "Ayşe Yılmaz", "email": "ayse@example.com" }],
  "repo": "https://github.com/your-team/your-builder",
  "commit": "the commit you ran",
  "run_command": "the command that runs your builder on this folder",
  "workflow": "submission/final.workflow.json",
  "trace": "traces/final.log",
  "mock_url": "https://your-mock.your-subdomain.workers.dev"
}
```

E-mail `submission.json`, the exported workflow and the trace to yavuz@freyavoice.ai before Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).

get confirmation# Mock service with Cloudflare Workers

Your flow's tools call a mock service that you write, instead of the real bank service. You publish this service as a free Cloudflare Worker. The `example/` folder here only shows the pattern: a Worker with a single endpoint (`POST /ping`). You will write the statement-debt services yourself.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or later
- A free Cloudflare account (dash.cloudflare.com)
- Wrangler (Cloudflare's command-line tool): runs without installing, via `npx wrangler ...`

## 1. Run the example locally

```bash
cd example
npx wrangler dev
```

The Worker opens at `http://localhost:8787`. Try it from another terminal:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8787/ping \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"kod": "A1"}'
```

The response is the same as `example/example-response.json`. For a code that does not exist it returns `404` and `{"hata": "kayıt bulunamadı"}`.

## 2. Publish it

```bash
npx wrangler login      # grant access to your Cloudflare account in the browser
npx wrangler deploy
```

The output shows the Worker address: `https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev`. To change the name, change the `name` field in `wrangler.toml`. Run `npx wrangler deploy` again whenever the code changes; the address stays the same.

Check after publishing:

```bash
curl -s https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/health
```

## 3. Connect the tool in the Freya flow to the Worker

1. Add an API tool to the flow.
2. Enter the method and address: `POST https://<your-worker-name>.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/<path>`. For the statement services, use the same path as under the bank's base address in `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` (for example `/voice/v1/cards.list`).
3. In the request body, write variables in the form `{{variable_name}}`. Example: `{"data": {"customerNo": "{{customerNumber}}", "aiFlow": "..."}, "call": {...}}`. During the call, the variable's value is substituted in.
4. Take the fields you will use in the flow from the response into variables.

The "Test API Request" button in the panel may send the text `{{customerNumber}}` as is, without filling in the variables. In this case the example Worker returns a valid record instead of an error (`isTemplateVariable`). Doing the same in your own services makes testing easier.

## When writing your own services

- Endpoints, request and response fields must match `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` exactly: the same path, the same field names (`data`/`call` request body, `data`/`result` response), the same date and amount format. The test customers' responses are in `../test-environment/test-customers.json`, explained in `../test-environment/test-customers.md`.
- Keep customer and card data in a table inside the Worker file (like `RECORDS` in the example). No database is needed.
- For a customer or card that is not found, return the error response from the contract; do not return made-up data.
- Responses should return data only (amount, date, status). The flow builds the sentence to be said to the customer.
- Do not put secret keys or real personal data in it; the Worker address is public.

# Credit cards: statements and payments

Answers to the questions we hear most often about your Yıldız credit card statement and how to pay it. Can't find what you need? Scroll to the bottom for ways to reach us.

---

**When will I get my statement?**

Once a month, on your statement date. Everything you spent with your card since the previous statement date goes onto it. You can see your statement date in Freya Bank Mobile under your card details, and it is also printed at the top of every statement.

**Can I change my statement date?**

Yes. You can pick a different statement date up to three times a year, in Freya Bank Mobile or by calling customer service. The new date applies from your next statement onwards. Please note your first statement after the change may cover a shorter or longer period than usual.

**How do I get my statement by e-mail?**

Just tell us where you'd like it sent. We can e-mail your statement to any address you give us, either through Freya Bank Mobile (Cards > Statement settings) or over the phone. E-mailed statements come as a PDF.

**I didn't receive my statement. What should I do?**

First check your spam or junk folder. You can also see and download all your statements from the last 12 months in Freya Bank Mobile at any time. If it's still missing, contact customer service and we'll send it again.

**What is the minimum payment?**

It is the smallest amount you need to pay by the due date to keep your card in good standing. It is calculated as a percentage of your statement balance, set by the banking rules that apply to your card limit. The exact amount is shown on your statement and in the app.

**What happens if I only pay the minimum?**

Your card stays in good standing, but interest is charged on the part of the balance you didn't pay. Paying the full statement balance is the only way to avoid interest.

**And if I pay less than the minimum, or nothing?**

Late payment interest is charged and it may affect your credit record. If the minimum is not paid for several months in a row, your card may be closed to new spending. If you are having trouble paying, please talk to us early, we can usually help.

**When is my payment due?**

Your due date is shown on your statement, usually about 10 days after the statement date. If the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday, it moves to the next working day.

**I spent in dollars, euros or pounds. How is that shown?**

Spending in a foreign currency is shown on your statement in that currency, separately from your Turkish lira spending. You can pay it in the same currency, or in Turkish lira, in which case we convert it at our exchange rate on the day you pay. Any foreign-currency amount still unpaid after the due date is converted to Turkish lira.

**How can I pay my card?**

- In Freya Bank Mobile: Cards > select your card > Pay. You can pay from any of your Freya Bank accounts.
- At any Freya Bank branch, in cash or from your account.
- At Freya Bank ATMs, with or without a card.
- Automatically: set up automatic payment and we'll take the minimum or the full amount from your account on the due date.

Payments in the app or at an ATM show on your card straight away. (Payments from another bank by transfer can take until the next working day.)

**Can I pay my card over the phone?**

You can check your balance and statement details on the phone line. For payments we recommend Freya Bank Mobile, it's the quickest way.

**Can I split my statement into instalments?**

For some purchases, yes, depending on the merchant and your card. Eligible transactions show an "Instalment" option in Freya Bank Mobile. Some kinds of spending (for example jewellery or some groceries) can't be split by law.

**There's a transaction on my statement I don't recognise. What do I do?**

Please contact customer service as soon as possible, by phone or through the "Messages" section in Freya Bank Mobile. Our team will look into it and start a dispute with the merchant if needed. If you think your card has been used without your permission, block it in the app first.

**Is my statement the same for all my cards?**

If you have more than one Yıldız card, each card gets its own statement, unless you have asked for a joint statement. Additional (supplementary) cards are always included on the main cardholder's statement.

# Voice assistant: statement and debt services, service contract

Author: Mert Koç, Integration Architecture, Freya Bank (mert.koc@freyabank.example)
Date: 1 October 2026
Distribution: Selin Aydın, Kerem Yalçın, Burcu Tan (Freya Bank); Deniz Arı (Freya)

> Mert: This is the contract the voice assistant integrates against for the statement / debt use case. It covers only the seven services the assistant calls. Everything about how the call reaches the assistant and how it goes back to the phone menu is Burcu's side and is not in here. If something below disagrees with what you see in the test environment, tell me and I'll check which side is wrong.

## 1. Before you start

- The caller is already identified when the assistant picks up. The phone menu hands over the **customer number** with the call, so there is no customer search service in this contract. Start from `cards.list`.
- Every service is `POST`, JSON in, JSON out, UTF-8.
- Base address for all seven:

```
https://api.freyabank.example/voice/v1/
```

  So the card list is `POST https://api.freyabank.example/voice/v1/cards.list`, and so on.
- Dates are strings in `dd.MM.yyyy` (e.g. `"05.11.2026"`). Amounts are JSON numbers with a dot as decimal separator (`5000.13`), never formatted strings. Do not round them.
- Turning numbers and dates into speech is the assistant's job. The services return raw values only, no sentences meant to be read to the caller (the `messageText` in errors is for logs, please don't read it out).

## 2. Access token

The services sit behind our API gateway. You need a bearer token first.

```
POST https://api.freyabank.example/oauth2/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=<client id>&client_secret=<client secret>&scope=voice.statement
```

Answer:

```json
{
  "access_token": "<token>",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 1800
}
```

Then on every service call:

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `Authorization` | `Bearer <token>` |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |
| `Accept` | `application/json` |

The token belongs to the integration (service account), not to the caller. Cache it and get a fresh one when it runs out; don't fetch one per call. Client id and secret: I'll send them over the secure channel, not by e-mail.

(Test environment: the token and headers are not checked there. Send them anyway so nothing changes when we switch.)

## 3. Envelope

### Request

```json
{
  "data": { "...service fields..." },
  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
}
```

`data` carries the fields of each service (section 5). `call` is call metadata we log on our side; nothing in this contract depends on it and the test environment ignores it.

### Response

Every answer has a `result` object. Successful answers also have `data`.

```json
{
  "data": { "...service fields..." },
  "result": {
    "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0002",
    "returnCode": "1",
    "messageText": "Success",
    "code": "1",
    "message": "Success",
    "type": null,
    "details": {
      "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0002",
      "rootCause": null,
      "errorOrigin": null
    }
  }
}
```

Success = HTTP 200 and `result.returnCode` is `"1"`. Anything else is an error, see section 4. `guid` is our trace id; if you open a ticket with us, give us the `guid`.

## 4. Errors

Error answers have **no `data` object**, only `result`:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0086",
    "returnCode": "FBE00099",
    "messageText": "Teknik hata: ABORTED: ",
    "code": "FBE00099",
    "message": "Teknik hata: ABORTED: ",
    "type": "ERROR",
    "details": {
      "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0086",
      "rootCause": "TechnicalError",
      "errorOrigin": "ivr-gateway-test:ivr-channel-v0"
    }
  }
}
```

`returnCode` and `code` always carry the same value, and so do `messageText` and `message`. `type` is `"ERROR"` or `"WARNING"`. `rootCause` and `errorOrigin` are diagnostic strings; log them, don't branch on them.

Codes you can get:

| HTTP | `code` | `type` | When | Services |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR` | `ERROR` | A required field is missing or empty (message names the field, e.g. `"card number cannot be empty"`) | all |
| 401 | (gateway) | | Token missing or expired. Get a new token and retry once | all |
| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_102` | `WARNING` | Customer has no valid card (message: `"Müşteriye ait geçerli kart bilgisi bulunamadı."`) | `cards.list` |
| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_120` | `WARNING` | Card not found | `cards.balance` |
| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_121` | `WARNING` | Card not found | `statement.week.get` |
| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_107` | `WARNING` | No statement document to send (message: `"Pdf dokümanı bulunamadı"`) | `statement.pdf.send` |
| 500 | `FBE00099` | `ERROR` | Technical error on our side (message: `"Teknik hata: ABORTED: "`) | all |

Note on the `cards.list` 404: it's a WARNING, it means "this customer has no card the assistant can work with", not that the service is broken. How the assistant reacts to that vs. a 500 is for Selin's analysis, I'm only flagging that they are different things.

Timeouts: we haven't agreed a client timeout yet. Most answers are well under a second, but under load (and once in the test data) an answer can take longer than ten seconds and still succeed. Open point, see section 7.

## 5. Services

| # | Service | Called with | Gives back |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.1 | `cards.list` | customer number | the customer's cards the assistant may talk about |
| 5.2 | `cards.balance` | card number | statement and due dates, debt per currency |
| 5.3 | `statement.week.get` | card number | the card's current statement week and day, joint statement info |
| 5.4 | `statement.week.decide` | card number + requested week | what the dates *would* be with that week (does not change anything) |
| 5.5 | `statement.week.change` | card number + requested week | changes the statement week |
| 5.6 | `contact.email.get` | customer number | registered e-mail / phone |
| 5.7 | `statement.pdf.send` | customer, card, currency, statement date, address | sends the statement PDF by e-mail |

Card number: always send the `cardNumber` **exactly as `cards.list` returned it**. Don't rebuild it from digits the caller says.

### 5.1 `cards.list`

Request:

```json
{
  "data": { "customerNo": "90000001", "aiFlow": "CardOps" },
  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
}
```

`customerNo` may be sent as a string or as a number, both are accepted. `aiFlow` tells us which use case is asking; for this one it's `"CardOps"` (not validated in test).

Response, one card:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "cards": [
      {
        "cardNumber": "540000******1234",
        "cardNumberLast4": "1234",
        "productName": "Yıldız Pratik Classic",
        "status": "A",
        "isMainCard": true
      }
    ],
    "validCardsCount": 1,
    "exitState": "1_CARD"
  },
  "result": { "returnCode": "1", "...": "as in section 3" }
}
```

Response, several cards (abridged):

```json
{
  "data": {
    "cards": [
      { "cardNumber": "540000******4253", "cardNumberLast4": "4253", "productName": "Yıldız Pratik", "status": "A", "isMainCard": true },
      { "cardNumber": "545000******4253", "cardNumberLast4": "4253", "productName": "Yıldız Pratik", "status": "A", "isMainCard": true },
      { "cardNumber": "540000******6184", "cardNumberLast4": "6184", "productName": "Yıldız Pratik", "status": "A", "isMainCard": true },
      { "cardNumber": "540000******8870", "cardNumberLast4": "8870", "productName": "Yıldız Tasarım", "status": "A", "isMainCard": true }
    ],
    "validCardsCount": 4,
    "exitState": "MULTI_CARD"
  },
  "result": { "returnCode": "1", "...": "" }
}
```

- `exitState`: `"1_CARD"` or `"MULTI_CARD"`.
- Only active cards come back (`status` `"A"`). `isMainCard` is `false` for a card that isn't the customer's own main card; it's still in the list.
- Two cards can have the same product name and the same last four digits (see above). Don't assume `cardNumberLast4` is unique.
- `productName` is free text from the card system, whatever was typed in there.
- Masking: in the **test environment** `cardNumber` comes back masked, first 6 and last 4 digits visible (`540000******1234`). What production returns in this field I still have to confirm with the card platform team; build so that it works with the masked form.

Errors: 404 `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_102`, 500 `FBE00099`.

### 5.2 `cards.balance`

Request:

```json
{
  "data": { "cardNumber": "540000******1234" },
  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
}
```

Response:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "cardNumber": "5400********1234",
    "cardNumberLast4": "1234",
    "productName": "Yıldız Pratik Classic",
    "statementDate": "05.10.2026",
    "lastPayDate": "15.10.2026",
    "nextStatementDate": "05.11.2026",
    "nextLastPayDate": "15.11.2026",
    "debtTL": {
      "statementPaymentStatus": "HAS_DEBT",
      "transferAmount": 0.0,
      "statementDebt": 5000.13,
      "minPayment": 2000.05,
      "remainingDebt": 5000.13,
      "remainingMinPayment": 2000.05,
      "currentPeriodExpense": 0.0,
      "totalDebt": 5000.13,
      "totalDebtPaymentStatus": "HAS_DEBT",
      "remainAutomaticPaymentAmount": 0.0
    },
    "debtUSD": {
      "statementPaymentStatus": "NO_DEBT",
      "transferAmount": 0.0,
      "statementDebt": 0.0,
      "minPayment": 0.0,
      "remainingDebt": 0.0,
      "remainingMinPayment": 0.0,
      "currentPeriodExpense": 0.0,
      "totalDebt": 0.0,
      "totalDebtPaymentStatus": "NO_DEBT",
      "remainAutomaticPaymentAmount": 0.0
    },
    "debtEUR": { "...": "same fields as debtUSD" },
    "debtGBP": { "...": "same fields as debtUSD" },
    "statementPaymentStatus": "HAS_DEBT",
    "totalDebtPaymentStatus": "HAS_DEBT",
    "automaticPaymentFlag": "N"
  },
  "result": { "returnCode": "1", "...": "" }
}
```

Field notes (my understanding from the card team, Selin please correct me if the business meaning is different):

- `statementDate` / `lastPayDate`: the last issued statement and its due date. `nextStatementDate` / `nextLastPayDate`: the coming ones.
- One block per currency: `debtTL`, `debtUSD`, `debtEUR`, `debtGBP`. **A block can be missing** (some cards have no GBP block at all). Missing block is not the same as a block with `NO_DEBT`; don't invent zeros for it.
- In each block: `statementDebt` is the statement debt, `minPayment` the minimum payment on the statement; `remainingDebt` / `remainingMinPayment` what is left of those after payments made since; `totalDebt` includes spending after the statement; `currentPeriodExpense` that spending; `transferAmount` carried over from the previous period.
- `statementPaymentStatus` / `totalDebtPaymentStatus`: `"HAS_DEBT"` or `"NO_DEBT"`, per block and once more at the top level for the card overall.
- `totalDebt` can be negative (credit balance on that currency). Status is `NO_DEBT` then.
- `automaticPaymentFlag`: `"Y"` / `"N"`. `remainAutomaticPaymentAmount` is only meaningful when it's `"Y"`.
- Heads-up: the `cardNumber` in this answer is masked differently from the card list (first 4 + last 4, `5400********1234`). Don't use it to match against the list; use `cardNumberLast4` or just keep the number you sent.

Errors: 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR` (empty card number), 404 `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_120`, 500 `FBE00099`. Example 404:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "guid": "<trace id>",
    "returnCode": "FB_IVR_CHANNEL_120",
    "messageText": "Kart bakiye servisi hatası: kart bulunamadı",
    "code": "FB_IVR_CHANNEL_120",
    "message": "Kart bakiye servisi hatası: kart bulunamadı",
    "type": "WARNING",
    "details": { "guid": "<trace id>", "rootCause": "NotFoundException", "errorOrigin": "<gateway>" }
  }
}
```

(The message text here is just my example; only the code matters.)

### 5.3 `statement.week.get`

Request:

```json
{
  "data": { "cardNumber": "540000******3201" },
  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
}
```

Response:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "cardNumber": "540000******3201",
    "cardNumberLast4": "3201",
    "productName": "Yıldız Pratik",
    "statementWeek": 3,
    "statementDay": 16,
    "statementDate": "16.10.2026",
    "lastPayDate": "26.10.2026",
    "nextStatementDate": "16.11.2026",
    "nextLastPayDate": "26.11.2026",

    "relatedCardNumber": "540000******3202",
    "relatedCardProductName": "Yıldız Premium"
  },
  "result": { "returnCode": "1", "...": "" }
```

(Taken from test customer 92220795, who has two cards on one statement.)

- `statementWeek`: 1 to 4, the week of the month the statement is cut. `statementDay`: day of the month. Both numbers here.
- `relationType`: empty string when the card has its own statement. `"M"` or `"C"` when two cards share one statement: `"M"` = this is the main card of the pair, `"C"` = this is the card linked to it. `relatedCardNumber` / `relatedCardProductName` then name the other card; otherwise they are empty strings. Changing the week on either card moves the shared statement, i.e. both cards.

### 5.4 `statement.week.decide`

Preview only. Tells you which statement date, due date and day the card would get with the requested week. **It does not change the card.**

Request:

```json

    "newStatementWeek": 2,
    "statementDay": 5
  },
  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
}
```

- `newStatementWeek`: 1-4, number or string both fine.
- `statementDay`: the card's current `statementDay` from `statement.week.get`.
- Asking for the week the card already has: there is nothing to preview, you'll get an error, so don't call it for that.

Response:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "statementDate": "09.11.2026",
    "statementDueDate": "19.11.2026",
    "statementDay": 9,
    "responseCode": 0,

  },
  "result": { "returnCode": "1", "...": "" }
```

`statementDate` / `statementDueDate` are the first statement and due date under the requested week. Note the due date is `statementDueDate` here, not `lastPayDate` like elsewhere (not my naming...). `responseCode` `0` = fine.

Errors: 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR`, 500 `FBE00099`.

### 5.5 `statement.week.change`

This one changes the card. Call it only after the caller has agreed to the dates from 5.4.

Request:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "cardNumber": "540000******1234",
    "newStatementWeek": 2,
    "statementDay": 5
  },
  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
}
```

`statementDay` is required by the request model even though the backend recalculates the day. Send the current day.

Response:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "responseCode": 0,
    "responseMessage": "00",
    "statementWeek": "2",
    "statementDay": "9",
    "exitState": "OK"
  },
  "result": { "returnCode": "1", "...": "" }
}
```

Careful: `statementWeek` and `statementDay` come back as **strings** here (numbers everywhere else). Ignore `statementDay` in this answer; the dates to tell the caller are the ones from 5.4. Success = `exitState` `"OK"` and `responseCode` `0`.

Errors: 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR`, 401 (token), 500 `FBE00099`.

### 5.6 `contact.email.get`

Request:

```json
{
  "data": { "customerNo": 90000001, "intAddressInfoType": "E" },
  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
}
```

`intAddressInfoType`: `"E"` e-mail, `"P"` phone, `"B"` both. Empty value gives a 400 (`"intAddressInfoType cannot be empty"`). The test environment returns the same answer whatever you ask for.

Response, e-mail registered:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "communicationType": "Both",
    "ibanCountryCode": "90",
    "ibanAreaCode": "500",
    "ibanPhoneNum": "0000000",
    "ibanEmail": "ornek@freyabank.example",
    "ttsEmail": "ornek@freyabank.example",
    "commGramType": "A",
    "exitState": "Done"
  },
  "result": { "returnCode": "1", "...": "" }
}
```

Response, only a phone registered:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "communicationType": "Phone",
    "ibanCountryCode": "90",
    "ibanAreaCode": "500",
    "ibanPhoneNum": "0000000",
    "ibanEmail": "",
    "ttsEmail": "",
    "commGramType": "A",
    "exitState": "Done"
  },
  "result": { "returnCode": "1", "...": "" }
}
```

- The registered e-mail is `ibanEmail`. `ttsEmail` is the same address prepared for reading aloud (today identical in practice).
- No registered e-mail = `communicationType` `"Phone"` and/or empty `ibanEmail`. Check the field, not only the type.
- The `iban*` prefix is historical, it has nothing to do with IBANs.

Errors: 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR`, 500 `FBE00099`.

### 5.7 `statement.pdf.send`

Sends the statement PDF to the address in the request.

Request:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "customerNo": "90000001",
    "cardNumber": "540000******1234",
    "currencyType": "TL",
    "statementDate": "05.10.2026",
    "emailAddress": "ornek@freyabank.example"
  },
  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
}
```

- `statementDate`: the `statementDate` from `cards.balance` (the issued statement).
- `currencyType`: `"TL"`, `"USD"`, `"EUR"` or `"GBP"`.
- `emailAddress`: the backend sends to whatever is in this field. It does **not** check it against the registered address. Whether any address other than the registered one is acceptable is a business/compliance question, Elçin and Selin's call, not mine.

Response:

```json
{
  "data": { "exitState": "DONE" },
  "result": { "returnCode": "1", "...": "" }
}
```

Errors: 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR`, 404 `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_107` (no PDF for that statement), 500 `FBE00099`. Example 404:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0466",
    "returnCode": "FB_IVR_CHANNEL_107",
    "messageText": "Pdf dokümanı bulunamadı",
    "code": "FB_IVR_CHANNEL_107",
    "message": "Pdf dokümanı bulunamadı",
    "type": "WARNING",
    "details": {
      "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0466",
      "rootCause": "com.freyabank.ivrgateway.ivrchannel.rest.exception.NotFoundException",
      "errorOrigin": "ivr-gateway-test:ivr-channel-v0"
    }
  }
}
```

## 6. Test environment

- Same paths and shapes as above. The synthetic customers and every answer they get are in `test-environment/test-customers.json` (overview in `test-environment/test-customers.md`). Nothing in there is a real person or card.
- If you build your own mock, it has to return those answers exactly (status code and body). For a customer or card that isn't in the file, return the 404 for that service from section 4 (for services without a 404 there, a 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR` body).
- Only the `data` fields decide the answer in test. Token, headers and `call` are not checked.

## 7. Open points (as of today)

1. Client timeout and retry policy: not agreed. My suggestion is no automatic retry on `statement.week.change` and `statement.pdf.send` (both have side effects).
2. Card number masking in production `cards.list`: confirming with the card platform team.
3. A flag for "can still change the statement week this year": asked, no answer.
4. Rate limits per client: will share when the gateway team sets them up. Shouldn't matter at pilot volume.

Mert
